material_findings.title: Restic plaintext blob hashes are incorrectly treated as exposed object-store identifiers

candidate_locators.exact: the store sees plaintext hashes, so (inference) a candidate chunk's presence is confirmable — identity doubles as a confirmation oracle.
Plaintext-hash IDs say yes, keyed/HMAC IDs say no. Test by hashing a known chunk and looking it up in a trial repository.

primary_locators.section: Repository Format, Pack Format, Unpacked Data Format, Indexing

material_findings.evidence_reasoning: The source distinguishes client plaintext blob IDs from storage IDs. The plaintext hashes in pack headers are available after decryption; headers and index files are encrypted/authenticated. Store-visible file names hash the stored encrypted file/pack bytes. An untrusted store with no repository password cannot perform the proposed raw-plaintext-hash lookup against the client index. A password-bearing client lookup would not establish a store-side oracle.
material_findings.materiality: This false failure boundary is a central shortlist discriminator, appears in the leakage comparison, and invalidates the stated oracle test for the Restic pattern. The brief specifically requires leakage and chunk-identity/encryption interaction.
material_findings.bounded_supported_meaning: Restic uses plaintext SHA-256 blob identity internally while protecting it in encrypted metadata. A hypothetical design publishing those plaintext IDs would create a dictionary oracle, but this is not the cited Restic design. Size/access-pattern attacks are separate and remain possible under their documented conditions.
material_findings.disposition: FAIL; preserve CDC, random-IV authenticated encryption and password re-wrap discoveries; do not reject Restic on the stated raw-hash exposure premise.

material_findings.title: The rotation drill equates encryption-key rotation with mandatory loss of cross-epoch deduplication

candidate_locators.exact: Distinguishes re-wrap-only rotation (cheap, keeps data keys) from true re-keying (expensive, breaks cross-epoch dedup).

primary_locators.section: Encryption: independent keys and ID/encryption formulas
Separate data/session keys and name keys

material_findings.evidence_reasoning: Borg explicitly separates id_key, enc_key and authentication keys; its object ID depends on id_key and plaintext, not enc_key. Thus changing enc_key alone does not mathematically invalidate plaintext chunk identities. Keeping an identity domain while replacing ciphertext is a design possibility, distinct from whether an existing CLI implements it and from the cost of rewriting old ciphertext. Tarsnap also separates per-archive/session encryption from stable HMAC naming and deduplicates across archives. Restic password changes do not revoke a leaked master key; the documented master-key replacement path is copy into a new repository or a new backup.
material_findings.materiality: The brief asks for ability to change an encryption key and rotation consequences. This binary prospective oracle incorrectly forces dedup loss as a consequence of every true encryption re-key and omits the identity-key/boundary-domain distinction that determines reuse.
material_findings.bounded_supported_meaning: Changing a keyed identity secret changes IDs; changing a chunker seed/polynomial can change boundaries; replacing encryption keys may require re-encryption or key-epoch handling without necessarily changing plaintext IDs. This assessment does not assert that Borg supplies an in-place re-key command, or that revoking an already leaked key can undo plaintext access to ciphertext the attacker retained.
material_findings.disposition: FAIL; retain the correct line-13/line-33 statement about id_key rotation and cheap passphrase re-wrap, without generalizing it to all encryption-key changes.

limitations.issue: Borg confidentiality condition is client concurrency/state, not user count. No cross-user sharing does not itself guarantee one independently updating client. Persistent trusted security state and safe CTR counter reservation also matter.
limitations.materiality: Scope qualification; no multi-client deployment is specified or required, so no invented deployment requirement or independent material failure is imposed.

limitations.issue: Per-archive AES session keys are evidenced, but archive-isolated blast radius is not established: archive lists reuse chunks, and the RSA unwrap key reaches session keys. The candidate does not explicitly claim complete archive isolation; the exact compromised-key subject remains unresolved.
limitations.materiality: Preserve as a bounded lead; not graded as a separately proven material falsehood.

limitations.issue: Restic implementation lead lacks an exact code URL; historical compression lead is valid, but unsupported older readers are rejected, so the compatibility inference must be version-bounded. Candidate explicitly says code was not inspected.
limitations.materiality: Locator/qualification limitations, not a requirement to inspect source code or implement a migration.

limitations.issue: CDC front-insert reuse is expected after resynchronization, not a guarantee of literally full reuse for every byte sequence. Restic nominal minimum has EOF-tail exceptions in the source. One file is a useful discriminating check, not proof that parameters are optimal for all workloads. Keyed IDs block a direct unkeyed dictionary comparison but do not hide all equality/access/size patterns.
limitations.materiality: No run or universal winner is claimed. These are bounded wording and future-test applicability qualifications.

useful_discoveries.description: Identity, encryption and wrapping key domains are separate decisions; Borg independent-key formulas expose which domain controls ID stability.

useful_discoveries.description: Tarsnap content-dependent chunkify.c uses HMAC-derived chunker parameters and a distinct content-cycle rule with a chosen-plaintext safeguard; this is a genuinely inspectable alternative to Restic Rabin boundaries.
